title: OTC Allowance Quarter-End Settlement (Pharmacy Benefit Operations Card)
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit — over-the-counter (OTC) allowance.** Once a benefit quarter has closed, its unused over-the-counter allowance is settled by one forfeiture entry tagged to that quarter.

### Business effect

The settlement adds one forfeiture entry to the allowance activity of the member's pharmacy coverage, tagged with the closed quarter and dated the day it is booked, and lowers the coverage's current allowance balance by the forfeited amount. Afterwards the allowance activity shows the forfeiture, and the balance no longer includes that money; whatever part of the quarter's unused allowance was not forfeited stays on the balance.

### How it is invoked

The settlement is an agent-side action. The agent unlocks the tool `forfeit_otc_quarter_0e0fa26e` and then calls it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `rx_coverage_id` | The reference number of the member's pharmacy coverage record, as returned by the pharmacy coverage lookup for the verified member | Identifier, as shown by the lookup |
| `benefit_quarter` | The closed calendar quarter the forfeiture belongs to | YYYY-Qn (for example 2026-Q1), exactly as the allowance activity tags that quarter's load |
| `forfeit_amount` | The allowance forfeited | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places; a value with more places is rounded to 2 decimal places |

### Return

On success the tool returns a text rendering of:

- `rx_otc_id` — the reference number of the new forfeiture entry;
- `benefit_quarter` — the quarter, YYYY-Qn;
- `forfeit_amount` — the amount booked, USD with 2 decimal places;
- `otc_balance` — the allowance balance after the forfeiture, USD with 2 decimal places;
- `status` — the text "forfeited", which confirms the entry was booked.

### Contract notes

*How many entries does one settlement create?* One forfeiture entry per call, tagged to the quarter given.

*What happens to the part of the unused allowance that is not forfeited?* It stays on the allowance balance.
